survivors.title: An approved dApp can reset its own spend caps and rate limiter: POST /wallet/session/close is not in the §4k first-party-only list
survivors.claim: 81c054c gates the permission surface by three exact path strings: `path.starts_with("/domain/permissions")`, `path == "/wallet/session-approve"`, `path == "/wallet/session-revoke"`. `/wallet/session/close` (slash, not hyphen) is not matched, so it is NOT refused for a page origin. domain_trust_gate returns Proceed unconditionally for `trust == "approved"` (request_gate.rs:807-809) and session_close has no gate of its own. `clear_session_for_browser` does `guard.remove(&browser_id)`, which drops spent_cents, payment_count_this_session AND payment_requests_this_minute in one call. So an approved dApp — reached by one ordinary 'approve this site' click, the most common action in the product — can, via wallet_call with endpoint `/wallet/session/close` and body `{"browser_id":N}`, erase the per-session spend cap ($10 default), the max-tx-per-session counter and the 60s rate limiter, then repeat. The page does not need to know its browser_id: the handler is idempotent (200 on unknown ids), so a loop over 0..N clears every tracked session.
survivors.why_it_matters: The per-session cap and rate limit are the only limits on a SILENT spend once a domain is approved. With them resettable on demand, an approved site can drain the wallet in unbounded silent increments of per_tx_limit_cents ($1 default), at unbounded rate. The only remaining user-facing signal is the gold pill. This is the exact defect shape §4k was written to close, missed for the exact reason the §4k comment warns about — enumerating by path string rather than gating a subtree.
survivors.how_to_confirm: Live: approve a test dApp, from its page call wallet_call('/wallet/session/close', {browser_id:<id>}, 'POST') and confirm a 200 + the log line '🛡️ session/close: cleared payment session counters'. Then make N silent payments each just under per_tx_limit_cents with a session/close between them and confirm total spend exceeds per_session_limit_cents with no prompt. NEGATIVE CONTROL: add `|| path == "/wallet/session/close"` to is_permission_surface, rebuild, re-run — the second payment must prompt (session_exceeded) and the close must 403.
survivors.refuter_reasoning:
Could not refute. All four citations are current and say exactly what the filer claims: main.rs:106-108 enumerates three exact path strings and /wallet/session/close (slash, not hyphen) matches none of them; main.rs:1167 registers the route; main.rs:1029 wraps domain_trust_mw App-wide so the middleware does see it and simply does not refuse it; request_gate.rs:807-809 is an unconditional `if trust == "approved" { return GateOutcome::Proceed; }`, mapped to next.call at main.rs:140-143; handlers.rs:171-192 has no gate of its own and its own comment at :164 states it is idempotent/200 on unknown ids; state.rs:507-513 is a single guard.remove(&browser_id) that drops spent_cents, payment_count_this_session and payment_requests_this_minute together.

Reachability verified end to end and no upstream gate exists: cefMessage is injected into external page contexts (simple_render_process_handler.cpp:733 ends the internal-only block, :735-741 creates it unconditionally); wallet_call is on the 4-name web-page allowlist (simple_handler.cpp:2046-2051); the endpoint is page-supplied and forwarded verbatim as hodos::WalletBaseUrl() + endpoint (simple_handler.cpp:2100, HttpRequestInterceptor.cpp:2077) with no endpoint allowlist anywhere in HandleIpcWalletCall (:2165-2209) or runIpcEngineCascade (:2025-2135) — isWalletEndpoint (:5103) governs only the direct-fetch Open() path; X-Requesting-Domain is stamped at :2069 so the approved->Proceed branch is taken. CORS is irrelevant on this transport (C++-side SyncHttpClient).

Refutations attempted and failed: (a) no persisted spend accumulator — request_gate.rs:1140-1149 sources session_spent_cents, payment_requests_this_minute and payment_count_this_session solely from get_session_counters_snapshot, and build_payment_context (context_builder.rs:156-197) reads only the limits from the DB row and all usage from those args, so removal genuinely zeroes all three; (b) session_close requires no C++-only header, browser_id comes from the JSON body; (c) no per-handler kind gate runs after Proceed for this handler.

Severity corrected CRITICAL -> HIGH for two reasons. First, an equivalent (noisier) reset already existed: counters key on browser->GetIdentifier(), and OnBeforePopup allows CEF_WOD_NEW_POPUP as a real window (simple_handler.cpp:1931-1934) and converts _blank/new-window to TabManager::CreateTab (:1945-1966), both minting a new browser id and hence a fresh zeroed counter bucket. This defect makes that silent and free — a real escalation, but not the line between bounded and unbounded spend. Second, the outcome is strictly weaker than the §4k defect it is compared to: per_tx_limit_cents still binds (it lives in the DB row and is NOT cleared), the gold pill still fires per payment (runIpcEngineCascade -> OnWalletCallSuccess, HttpRequestInterceptor.cpp:2124), and each tx costs the 1000-sat service fee, so a drain requires hundreds to thousands of visible transactions rather than one silent unlimited one. Precondition is also a genuine one: trust must already be "approved".

Two minor corrections to the write-up, neither load-bearing: the 0..N loop is unnecessary (the payment gate uses the C++-stamped X-Browser-Id, i.e. the attacker's own tab), and "the per-session cap and rate limit are the only limits" understates it — per_tx_limit_cents also binds and survives, which is why the drain is incremental.

Label check: filed as CODE_READING and it is one. I ran nothing, opened no browser, sent no transaction. Fix shape should gate the subtree (e.g. mutating path.starts_with("/wallet/session")) rather than adding a fourth string, per the main.rs:96-99 comment's own warning.

survivors.title: A decoy empty "outputs" key prices /transaction/send, peerpay/send and paymail/send at 0 cents, silently auto-approving any amount
survivors.claim: ExtractOutputSatoshis tests `json.contains("outputs") && json["outputs"].is_array()` FIRST and returns from that branch unconditionally. A body `{"outputs":[], "toAddress":"1...", "amount":100000000}` therefore returns 0 and never reaches the sendMax/amount/amount_satoshis branches. ComputePaymentCost then sets satoshis=0, cents=0, priceAvailable=true (PaymentCost.h:116-121). Rust's SendTransactionRequest is a plain `#[derive(Deserialize)]` with no deny_unknown_fields, so serde silently ignores the decoy `outputs` key and executes the real `amount`. dispatch_payment_with_amount takes resolved_amount=None when send_max is false (handlers.rs:9700-9730), so the header values win, and build_payment_context(0 cents, price_available=true) hits matrix_c's SilentWithinCaps — asserted by the engine's own test bsv_price_available_with_zero_cents_is_silent. Same for /wallet/peerpay/send and /wallet/paymail/send, which use plain dispatch_payment (handlers.rs:17228, 18279) with no resolved amount. The existing unit test file cef-native/tests/payment_cost_test.cpp does not cover a body carrying BOTH `outputs` and an amount field.
survivors.why_it_matters: 32680f1 and 9dc1586 exist precisely to put a cap gate on these three fund-movers. This defeats it: an approved dApp moves an arbitrary amount to an arbitrary address with no modal. Worse, the gold pill still fires (isPaymentKind is true regardless of the decoy) but reports 0 cents — the safeguard displays $0.00 over a full-balance send. PaymentCost.h's own header comment names this consequence: 'prices the call at 0 cents, which the engine reads as under every cap and SILENTLY AUTO-APPROVES'.
survivors.how_to_confirm: Cheapest first: add a GTest to cef-native/tests/payment_cost_test.cpp asserting ExtractOutputSatoshis(R"({\"outputs\":[],\"toAddress\":\"1abc\",\"amount\":100000000})") == 100000000 and watch it fail with 0. Then live, on a testnet-value amount from an approved test dApp: send the decoy body to /transaction/send and confirm no modal + a 0-cent gold pill + the real amount broadcast. NEGATIVE CONTROL: send the same body without the `outputs` key and confirm the payment_confirmation modal appears.
survivors.refuter_reasoning:
Could not refute; every cited location is current and says what is claimed.

VERIFIED CHAIN (all CODE_READING, no build/run):
1. PaymentCost.h:55-63 — the `outputs`/is_array branch is tested FIRST and `return total;` is unconditional. `{"outputs":[],"toAddress":"1...","amount":N}` returns 0; the sendMax/amount/amount_satoshis arms (:67-78) are unreachable for that body. ComputePaymentCost (:110-122) then yields satoshis=0, cents=0, priceAvailable=(bsvPriceUsd>0)=TRUE under a live feed. Cited range 49-84 exact.
2. handlers.rs:9608-9617 SendTransactionRequest is a bare derive. `grep -rc deny_unknown_fields rust-wallet/src` = 0 across the whole crate, so serde drops the decoy `outputs` and executes `amount` (:9639, :9746, :9756-9764).
3. request_gate.rs:919-949 PaymentCall::from_headers trusts X-Payment-Cents / X-Bsv-Price-Available verbatim; the resolved-amount override (:1106-1114) applies only when Some, and handlers.rs:9700-9730 builds it ONLY in the `if send_max` arm. So sendMax is protected; a plain `amount` is not.
4. Production branch confirmed, not just the test: matrix_c.rs::decide_payment (:216-289) — PriceUnavailable guard at :240 needs !bsv_price_available (skipped); :273 `0 > per_tx_limit` false; :281 `0+0 > per_session_limit` false; -> SilentWithinCaps at :289.
5. WEB-PAGE REACHABLE via two independent transports. (a) simple_render_process_handler.cpp:586,733,736-741 gives every external page `cefMessage`; simple_handler.cpp:2046-2051 allowlists `wallet_call`; :2100 takes the endpoint as an arbitrary page-supplied string with NO route allowlist; HttpRequestInterceptor.cpp:2207 -> runIpcEngineCascade:2037 prices the page body, :2070-2074 stamps headers. (b) plain fetch(): isWalletEndpoint :5124 `/transaction/` and :5123 `/wallet/`; Open() prices at :2293-2298, injects at :3615-3623. Precondition is trust_level=approved — the normal post-connect state and exactly what the caps exist to bound, not a mitigation.
6. No downstream backstop: send_transaction's inner create_action is deliberately header-less (:9800-9801) so the second gate sees an internal request; check_domain_approved (:621-661) is trust-level only, takes no amount, and none of the three handlers calls it.
7. The x-payment- prefix strip at :3667 is intact but irrelevant — the page does not forge headers, it makes C++ compute them wrongly.

THREE AMPLIFICATIONS THE FILER MISSED (all worsen it):
- "Always notify" is also defeated: zeroed limits give per_tx_limit_cents=0 and `0 > 0` is false -> Silent; max_tx_per_session=0 disables its own guard (:263). The cautious-user opt-in offers no protection against this body.
- Repeatable: record_spending (:1166) records 0 cents so the session dollar cap never accumulates; bounds are only rate_limit_per_min=30 and max_tx_per_session=100 (migrations.rs:475-476) — up to 100 unlimited-amount silent sends per session.
- 32680f1 is a NET REGRESSION: `git show 32680f1^` shows the old extractOutputSatoshis returned 0 for any non-outputs body and these routes were absent from isPaymentEndpoint, so external callers arrived header-less and request_gate.rs:1087-1101 fail-closed into a PriceUnavailable PROMPT. Before the commit the attacker got a modal; after it, silence. The comments still asserting the old fail-closed behavior (handlers.rs:9678-9686, :17223-17227, :18276-18278) are now stale and misleading.

CITATION CORRECTION (imprecision, not mislabelling): matrix_c.rs:782-795 is the TEST bsv_price_available_with_zero_cents_is_silent, not the branch; the branch is :216-289. The finding's prose describes it as the engine's own test, so this is fair.

LABELLING: correctly labelled CODE_READING; no measurement was claimed.

SEVERITY: checked for inflation and found the opposite. CRITICAL stands.

CAVEAT: unmeasured end-to-end. The two relied-on behaviors (nlohmann `[]`.is_array()==true; serde ignoring unknown fields absent deny_unknown_fields) are standard and documented, but no compiler was available here (no g++/cl; nlohmann is vcpkg-provided, not vendored). Confidence high, not certain-by-measurement. Decisive cheap test: add to cef-native/tests/payment_cost_test.cpp an assertion that ExtractOutputSatoshis(R"({"outputs":[],"toAddress":"1abc","amount":50000})") == 50000 — today it returns 0, and the existing file (:52-89) provably does not cover it, since `{"outputs":"not an array"}` is a string and therefore falls through to the very branches the array case skips.

survivors.title: The C1 fail-closed origin cascade was applied only to the IPC transport — HttpRequestInterceptor::extractDomain still yields an empty domain, which both C++ and Rust read as fully-trusted wallet-internal
survivors.location: cef-native/src/core/HttpRequestInterceptor.cpp:5173-5215 (extractDomain) + :1016-1025 (IsInternalOrigin, empty==true) + :2240-2246 (Open() internal bypass) + :3597-3600 (X-Requesting-Domain only when non-empty) + rust-wallet/src/main.rs:64-75 (absent header => no gate)
survivors.claim: aa439d3 (C1) touched only PortConfig.h and simple_handler.cpp — `git show aa439d3 --stat` confirms HttpRequestInterceptor.cpp is not in the diff. extractDomain retains the pre-C1 shape: an unanchored `find("://")` on browser->GetMainFrame()->GetURL(), no scheme anchor, no userinfo strip, no ancestor cascade, and no opaque-origin sentinel — it simply leaves `domain` empty. Empty domain then means (a) IsInternalOrigin("") returns true so Open() takes the 'Internal origin — bypassing domain check' early return, and (b) startAsyncHTTPRequest omits X-Requesting-Domain entirely, so domain_trust_mw takes its `None => next.call(req)` branch and every per-handler kind gate (dispatch_payment included) also returns Proceed on a missing header. Result: a fully ungated fund-moving call on the direct-fetch transport. Reachability I believe but have not run: OnBeforePopup (simple_handler.cpp:1923-1926) returns false for `url.empty()` and for CEF_WOD_NEW_POPUP, so `window.open('','_blank','popup')` produces a real, opener-scriptable popup whose main frame URL is `about:blank`; extractDomain finds no '://' and the referrer fallback for an about:blank document is empty. A fetch from that popup to http://127.0.0.1:31301/transaction/send (or now http://127.0.0.1:3321/... via 9b73bd7) is intercepted and forwarded header-free. Note this transport is not defended by CORS: the interceptor re-issues the request as a fresh CefURLRequest with the page Origin stripped (d0ee6db) and http://127.0.0.1:31301 explicitly allowlisted, so it is CORS-clean by construction — X-Requesting-Domain is the ONLY thing separating it from full trust.
survivors.why_it_matters: C2's default-deny gate closed the IPC transport, but the direct-fetch transport is the one @bsv/sdk WalletClient actually uses by default, and 9b73bd7 just widened it to three more ports in both host spellings. The exact bug class C1 was written to kill — 'manufacturing an empty origin for a frame that HAS a security origin' — still lives on the money path, one file over. History shows this was once closed and reverted (5de4a62 / ccf7c6d, 'B2 lockdown - reject external direct-fetch wallet calls').
survivors.how_to_confirm: Two steps, and do the first even if you doubt the second. (1) CODE: confirm no caller re-derives the domain — grep shows extractDomain is the sole producer of requestDomain_ (call sites :3846, :3979). (2) LIVE, read-only endpoint first so no money moves: from https://example.com run `var w=window.open('','_blank','width=200,height=200'); w.document.write('<script>fetch("http://127.0.0.1:31401/wallet/balance").then(r=>r.text()).then(t=>opener.postMessage(t,"*"))<\/script>')` and look for '🔒 Internal origin  — bypassing domain check' with an EMPTY origin in the browser log. If that line appears, the bypass is proven without spending anything. NEGATIVE CONTROL: same fetch from the top-level example.com frame must log the domain 'example.com' and be gated.
survivors.refuter_reasoning:
REFUTATION FAILED — the finding survives. Every cited location is current and says what is claimed.

VERIFIED, hop by hop:
- `git show aa439d3 --stat`: touches only PortConfig.h, simple_handler.cpp, tests/CMakeLists.txt, tests/port_config_origin_test.cpp. HttpRequestInterceptor.cpp is NOT in the C1 diff. Confirmed.
- HttpRequestInterceptor.cpp:5173-5214 `extractDomain` — verbatim as described: unanchored `mainFrameUrl.find("://")`, no scheme anchor, no userinfo strip, no ancestor cascade, no sentinel; leaves `domain` empty and returns it.
- :1016-1017 `bool IsInternalOrigin(...) { if (origin.empty()) return true; ...}` — confirmed, with an in-code comment that says empty "falls back to wallet-internal trust".
- :2240-2246 `Open()` — `if (IsInternalOrigin(requestDomain_)) { LOG "Internal origin — bypassing domain check"; handle_request = true; CefPostTask(StartAsyncHTTPRequestTask); return true; }`. Confirmed.
- :3598-3601 (finding said 3597-3600) `if (!requestDomain_.empty()) headers.insert("X-Requesting-Domain", ...)`. Confirmed.
- rust-wallet/src/main.rs:65-76 `domain_trust_mw` — `.filter(|s| !s.is_empty())` then `None => return Ok(next.call(req).await?...)`. Confirmed.
- rust-wallet/src/permission_service/request_gate.rs:1026-1034 `dispatch_payment_with_amount` — `None => return GateOutcome::Proceed`. So even the new finding-6 payment gate on /transaction/send proceeds unconditionally without the header. Confirmed.
- The asymmetry is exact and deliberate-looking: `ResolveIpcOrigin` (simple_handler.cpp:2008-2030) has scheme-anchored `hodos::OriginFromUrl` + ancestor cascade + `opaque-origin.invalid` sentinel. `extractDomain` has none of the three, and grep shows zero callers of `OriginFromUrl` in HttpRequestInterceptor.cpp.

UPSTREAM GATES I HUNTED FOR AND DID NOT FIND:
- simple_handler.cpp:8035 GetResourceRequestHandler installs HttpRequestInterceptor for every role EXCEPT wallet/wallet_panel/settings/backup (:8070-8075). A popup inherits the opener's SimpleHandler, so role_ is the tab's — not exempt. Confirmed at :8187-8195 (wallet host/port + the three foreign bridge ports -> `new HttpRequestInterceptor()`).
- `hodos::IsInternalFrontendUrl` is :5137-only (PortConfig.h:137-140), so :31301 is not short-circuited to disk.
- Nothing between `isWalletEndpoint` (:3898) and handler construction (:3984) checks origin.
- OnBeforePopup :1922-1926 (`url.empty()`) and :1933-1936 (CEF_WOD_NEW_POPUP) both `return false` = allow. No popup gate in OnAfterCreated / OnBeforeClose.

MY BEST OBJECTION, WHICH I KILLED MYSELF: I expected CORS preflight on a cross-origin POST with application/json to block this. It does not. GetResponseHeaders (:1420-1423) sets `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`, `Access-Control-Allow-Methods: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, OPTIONS`, AND `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Content-Type, Authorization`. Preflight succeeds by construction. Independently corroborated by commit e0cebd9 ("the C++ interceptor serves Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * ... external dApps using the @bsv/sdk WalletClient HTTP substrate direct-fetch localhost:31301 successfully and commonly"), which also confirms the finding's 5de4a62 / ccf7c6d history citation verbatim (`fix(cef): B2 lockdown - reject external direct-fetch wallet calls` and its Revert).

EVIDENCE THE FILER MISSED THAT STRENGTHENS THE FINDING:
1. PHASE_CONTRACT.md:220-223 records WHY `IsInternalOrigin("")` was left alone: "it is also fed by the HTTP path, where an absent X-Requesting-Domain legitimately means internal." That is layer-confused. On the HTTP path IsInternalOrigin is fed by extractDomain's C++ return value; the absent-header rule is a separate Rust check. The recorded justification does not describe the code it justifies.
2. PHASE_CONTRACT.md:775 defers ONLY "extractDomain()'s scheme-blindness and main-frame-URL sourcing." The empty-origin / missing-sentinel property is in neither that deferral nor named residuals 7, 8 or 9. Under HARNESS section 4, an unnamed residual is a defect, not a baseline.

CORRECTIONS TO THE FINDING (none fatal):
- "9b73bd7 just widened it to three more ports" is overstated. Intercepting 3321/2121/8080 grants the attacker no new capability for THIS bug; 127.0.0.1:31301 was always directly addressable.
- A second vector exists that needs neither a popup nor any unverified Chromium behavior: a file:// main frame. "file:///C:/x.html" -> find("://")=4, domainStart=7, first '/' at index 7 -> substr(7,0) = EMPTY. Same bypass via a user opening a downloaded HTML file. My own CODE_READING, medium confidence (did not verify Hodos permits file:// navigation).
- Cited line numbers off by 0-2 in two of five citations (:3597-3600 is :3598-3601; popup arms are :1922-1926 and :1933-1936). Immaterial.

WHAT IS GENUINELY UNPROVEN: only the LAST hop — that an opener-scripted `window.open('','_blank','popup')` browser reports a main-frame URL containing no "://" at fetch time and carries an empty Referer. The filer states this honestly as unrun. A prior panel reached the identical popup reading (ADVERSARIAL_PANEL_2026-08-19.md:159, finding 8) but two agreeing code readings are not a measurement. Falsification test: log extractDomain's result plus browser->GetMainFrame()->GetURL() for a fetch from such a popup; a non-empty domain kills the exploit while the design defect survives.

LABEL: claimed CODE_READING, and it is one. Not mislabelled.

SEVERITY: HIGH is correct and arguably conservative. The full mechanism is confirmed and the direct-fetch transport is documented as live and heavily used; only the final reachability hop is unmeasured, which is the sole reason I do not raise this to CRITICAL.

survivors.title: With one approval click a dApp reaches ungated destructive and fund-moving routes: /wallet/delete, /wallet/backup/onchain, /wallet/consolidate-dust, /shutdown, /wallet/reveal-mnemonic
survivors.location: rust-wallet/src/permission_service/request_gate.rs:804-809 (approved => Proceed for any endpoint) + rust-wallet/src/handlers.rs:2853 (wallet_delete), :12805 (wallet_backup_onchain), :16854 (wallet_consolidate_dust), :193 (shutdown), :18957 (reveal_mnemonic) + cef-native/src/core/HttpRequestInterceptor.cpp:2069-2078 (endpoint concatenated with no allowlist)
survivors.claim: wallet_call forwards a page-supplied endpoint + method + body verbatim (`std::string url = hodos::WalletBaseUrl() + endpoint;`, HttpRequestInterceptor.cpp:2078) with no allowlist, and domain_trust_gate short-circuits to Proceed for any approved domain on any endpoint. Grepping X-Requesting-Domain in handlers.rs shows the first-party-only guard exists on exactly four handlers — wallet_backup (:12673), wallet_restore (:15050), wallet_export (:16907), wallet_import (:16990). It does NOT exist on: wallet_delete (destroys the wallet; its only precondition is no pending txs, and it first spends funds on an on-chain backup), wallet_backup_onchain (broadcasts a funded tx), wallet_consolidate_dust (moves UTXOs and pays the 1000-sat treasury fee via task_consolidate_dust::run_inner), shutdown (kills the wallet process), or reveal_mnemonic. reveal_mnemonic returns the BIP39 phrase to the caller with no domain check: it requires a correct PIN only when db.is_pin_protected() is true, and on the `else` branch (legacy / DPAPI-only, no pin_salt) it returns the mnemonic to any caller whenever the wallet is unlocked. Even PIN-protected, it is an unrate-limited PIN oracle callable from page context.
survivors.why_it_matters: §4k correctly identified that 'approved' is a low bar granted by the product's most common click, then fixed only the permission table. The same one-click grant still buys wallet destruction, unauthorised spends outside the payment gate entirely (consolidate-dust and on-chain backup are not payment endpoints, so no cap, no counter, no gold pill), a wallet-process DoS, and — on any wallet without a PIN salt — the recovery phrase.
survivors.how_to_confirm: Static: `grep -n 'X-Requesting-Domain' rust-wallet/src/handlers.rs` and diff the guarded set against the fund-moving/destructive route list in main.rs:1032-1205. Live, on a throwaway profile only: from an approved test dApp call wallet_call('/wallet/consolidate-dust','{}','POST') and confirm a 200 with a txid and no modal. Do NOT test /wallet/delete against a funded wallet. NEGATIVE CONTROL: add the same X-Requesting-Domain reject block that wallet_export uses, rebuild, confirm 403.
survivors.refuter_reasoning:
COULD NOT REFUTE. Independently confirmed end-to-end; correctly labelled CODE_READING (filer ran nothing, neither did I).

CITATIONS CURRENT: request_gate.rs:807 is `if trust == "approved" { return GateOutcome::Proceed; }`. HttpRequestInterceptor.cpp:2076 is `std::string url = hodos::WalletBaseUrl() + endpoint;` (filer said :2078, inside their own cited 2069-2078 range). All five handlers land exactly on the claimed `pub async fn`: handlers.rs:193 shutdown, :2853 wallet_delete, :12805 wallet_backup_onchain, :16854 wallet_consolidate_dust, :18957 reveal_mnemonic. Routes at main.rs:1033/1097/1119/1128/1204, all under the single flat App::new() wrapped by domain_trust_mw at main.rs:1029. The four first-party-guarded handlers are exactly the four named (wallet_backup :12673, wallet_restore :15050, wallet_export :16907, wallet_import :16990); a 5th X-Requesting-Domain use at :17704 is pay_402, not one of the five.

NO UPSTREAM GATE EXISTS. (a) `wallet_call` IS on the 4-name web-page allowlist, simple_handler.cpp:2046-2051. (b) HandleIpcWalletCall (HttpRequestInterceptor.cpp:2165-2209) checks internal-origin / wallet-exists / trust and never inspects `endpoint`. (c) dispatchWalletHttpByMethod (:1890) accepts any verb via SyncHttpClient::Request. (d) Rust middleware's only endpoint-aware arm is the new §4k permission-surface refusal; all else falls to domain_trust_gate -> Proceed, with no rate limit on the approved path. (e) The isWalletEndpoint route table gates only the direct-fetch transport; the IPC transport builds its own URL and never consults it. (f) CORS is irrelevant — the C++ SyncHttpClient call carries only Content-Type / X-Requesting-Domain / X-Payment-*, no Origin.

REACHABILITY IS BY WEB PAGE, not local code execution. CWIShimScript.h:197 defines `window.__hodos_walletCall(method, endpoint, body, httpMethod)` as a plain writable global accepting an ARBITRARY endpoint and resolving with the response body, injected on external https main frames (simple_render_process_handler.cpp ~789-799) — exactly the page class that gets "approved". One line: `await window.__hodos_walletCall('x','/wallet/reveal-mnemonic',{pin:'0000'},'POST')`. AMPLIFICATION THE FILER MISSED: cefMessage is bound in EVERY frame (:737) and the destructive endpoints are fire-and-forget, so /wallet/delete and /shutdown are reachable from any subframe of the approved origin.

SEVERITY RAISED TO CRITICAL — the filer UNDER-stated it. They dismissed the PIN case as "an unrate-limited PIN oracle". The PIN is 4 DIGITS (crypto/pin.rs:3; WalletPanelPage.tsx:172 `['','','','']`) = 10,000 keyspace; grep for lockout|pin_attempts|failed_pin|too_many_attempts across rust-wallet/src returns NOTHING; 600k PBKDF2 iterations (pin.rs:17) is the only brake; plaintext is returned to page JS. Sending `'[]'` instead forces `HideWalletOverlay()` + `StartQRScreenCapture()` (:4227-4236), letting a page dismiss the wallet overlay and start a screen-capture selection.
survivors.why_it_matters: This is a payment-address substitution on the money path. A user who scans a QR to pay someone sees a prefilled, plausible-looking form and confirms it; the address swap is exactly the class of attack QR scanning exists to avoid. The 'user must still confirm' mitigation assumes the user re-reads a 34-character base58 string they believe the scanner just produced for them.
survivors.how_to_confirm: Load a page whose only script is `setInterval(()=>cefMessage.send('qr_found',[JSON.stringify([{type:'address',value:'1BurnAddr...'}])]),5)`, open the wallet, click Scan QR, and observe whether the send form opens prefilled with the attacker address rather than with any QR actually on the page. Negative control: put a real BSV QR image on the same page with the interval disabled and confirm the genuine value arrives.

survivors.title: HttpRequestInterceptor::GetResourceHandler mutates the request via SetURL, which the CEF contract forbids — so either the 9b73bd7 scheme-downgrade is dead code and its MEASURED evidence is void, or it is a page-triggerable HTTPS-strip on unrelated third-party requests
survivors.location: cef-native/src/core/HttpRequestInterceptor.cpp:3745-3778 (redirectPort + downgrade, four request->SetURL calls); cef-binaries/include/cef_resource_request_handler.h:104; cef-native/src/core/HttpRequestInterceptor.cpp:3593 (the actual outbound URL)
survivors.claim: The CEF header states of GetResourceHandler: 'The |request| object cannot not be modified in this callback' (cef_resource_request_handler.h:104). Independently of whether SetURL is silently dropped, the outbound wallet call is built from scratch as `hodos::WalletBaseUrl() + endpoint_` (HttpRequestInterceptor.cpp:3593), and WalletBaseUrl() is hardcoded `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` (PortConfig.h:44). Therefore the https->http downgrade at :3773-3777 cannot be what stopped an 'https client against our plaintext wallet dying in the TLS handshake' — that outbound request was never https. The commit's GREEN evidence for its defect 2 is four LOG_DEBUG_HTTP lines printed immediately BEFORE each SetURL (:3758, :3775), which print identically whether or not SetURL takes effect: the test passes with the feature removed. Defect 3 (/health absent from isWalletEndpoint) fully explains the pre-fix 'Bridge unavailable' symptom on its own. The branch that matters for harm: entry into this handler is `hodos::IsLoopbackHostPort(url, port)` (PortConfig.h:180-183), an UNANCHORED substring search, called from simple_handler.cpp:8187-8192. So `https://victim.example/anything?q=localhost:8080` enters the interceptor, `redirectPort` rewrites the query substring to `localhost:31301` (:3745-3762), and the downgrade then fires because IsWalletHostPort is now satisfied. If SetURL is ever effective on this path, that is a silent HTTPS->HTTP downgrade plus query-string rewrite of an unrelated site's request, triggerable by any link, iframe or img src.
survivors.why_it_matters: Two ways to lose. If the code is dead, a future reader will rely on a rewrite that never happens (and the commit message enshrines a wrong root cause for the next person debugging bridge interop). If it is live, a substring anywhere in a URL strips TLS from a third-party request and sends its cookies in the clear. Nobody looked, because the logging cannot distinguish the two.
survivors.how_to_confirm: Add a temporary log of `request->GetURL()` immediately AFTER each SetURL in GetResourceHandler and compare with the value logged before it; or point a dev build at a local https server and load `https://<that server>/x?q=localhost:8080` while watching the wire. If the URL is unchanged after SetURL, the downgrade is dead code and 9b73bd7's defect-2 evidence must be withdrawn.
survivors.refuter_reasoning:
SUBJECT PROVEN: cef-binaries/include/cef_version.h:38 = 150.0.43-7871.3576+g9ccef04; the local tree /c/cef/cef150/chromium/src/cef is at HEAD 9ccef044f (same commit), and cef-binaries ships Release/ only. The libcef source read below is the source of the linked binary.

It cannot be, by two independent mechanisms in the shipped source. libcef/browser/net_service/resource_request_handler_wrapper.cc:780 copies pending_request_ back into the real request, :790 sets SetReadOnly(true), :791 SetTrackChanges(false), and only then :812 calls handler_->GetResourceHandler(). CefRequestImpl::SetURL (libcef/common/request_impl.cc:201-209) begins with CHECK_READONLY_RETURN_VOID(), defined at request_impl.cc:164-168 as `if (read_only_) { DCHECK(false); return; }`. out/Release_GN_x64/args.gn sets is_official_build=true with NO dcheck_always_on (only Debug_GN_* set it), so DCHECK compiles out and SetURL silently early-returns. Even absent that, copy-back already happened and change tracking is off, so nothing could propagate. Consequently https://victim.example/anything?q=localhost:8080 proceeds to the network as https:// with its original query intact. No TLS strip, no third-party query rewrite, no cookie exposure. The scenario does not exist.

DEAD-CODE HALF — CONFIRMED, with stronger evidence than the filer had. The three request->SetURL calls in HttpRequestInterceptor::GetResourceHandler (HttpRequestInterceptor.cpp:3758, :3776, :3815) are inert. All downstream behavior is driven by the local std::string url, which IS rewritten and IS what feeds isWalletEndpoint()/endpoint extraction — that is why re-pointing works. The outbound call is rebuilt from scratch at HttpRequestInterceptor.cpp:3588 (hodos::WalletBaseUrl() + endpoint_), and WalletBaseUrl() is hardcoded http://127.0.0.1:<port> at PortConfig.h:44. So 9b73bd7's defect-2 root cause ("an https client against our plaintext wallet, dead in the TLS handshake") cannot have been the mechanism: the incoming scheme never reaches an outbound socket on the intercepted path, and the local-string downgrade is behaviorally a no-op too (http:// and https:// parse identically for the find("://") path extraction at :3805-3812). Given this project's documented cost from enshrined wrong root causes, that is the finding worth keeping.

FILER'S ERRORS: (1) :3593 is wrong — the WalletBaseUrl()+endpoint_ line is :3588. (2) "four request->SetURL calls" in 3745-3778 is wrong — that range holds TWO statements (:3758 in the redirectPort lambda, :3776 the downgrade), three dynamic invocations; a third statement is outside the range at :3815. (3) "Defect 3 fully explains the pre-fix symptom on its own" is overstated — defect 1 (host-form gap, simple_handler.cpp:8187-8192 / PortConfig.h:180-183) was independently load-bearing, since the 127.0.0.1 spelling never entered the interceptor at all. Their narrower point (defect 2 was not load-bearing) stands. (4) "The test passes with the feature removed" is true of defect 2 only, not of the commit: 9b73bd7's evidence block also contains a wallet-side end-to-end measurement (POST /getVersion 200 221, banner "Bridge unavailable" -> "Connected") against a paired RED. Only the four rewrite log lines as evidence FOR defect 2's mechanism are void — they print at :3757 and :3775, immediately before each dead SetURL, and would print identically with the downgrade block deleted.

LABELING: correct. They claimed CODE_READING and it is one. Not mislabelled.

PANEL QUESTIONS: (a) Could the commit's defect-2 evidence pass with the feature removed? Yes — refutes that sub-claim's evidence, not the commit's overall evidence. (b) Subject proven above by version+commit match, not asserted. (c) If the harm branch were real you would see an http:// request to a third-party host in a network capture; nobody looked, and my source reading shows it cannot occur. (d) My verdict is a CODE_READING of libcef and app source plus a read of args.gn; I ran no browser and sent no transaction.

Interop-only, no money or trust-boundary impact.

ADJACENT LEAD, NOT CONFIRMATION OF THIS FINDING (separate, low confidence, CODE_READING): hodos::IsLoopbackHostPort and every isWalletEndpoint path arm are unanchored find(). After redirectPort rewrites the local string, https://victim.example/wallet/x?q=localhost:8080 satisfies IsWalletHostPort and isWalletEndpoint, so AsyncWalletResourceHandler is built and the wallet response is delivered to the page as if from its own origin; isSocketIOConnection (:5162-5171) is reachable the same way. This needs no working SetURL and deserves its own investigation — I am not confirming it here.

SEVERITY: the surviving defect is dead code plus a wrong root cause recorded in a commit message, largely pre-existing (the redirectPort SetURL dates to 29c8e3a/4ba4fe7, well before this range; 9b73bd7 added one more inert call and the incorrect comment). Zero security impact, zero regression on the money path. MEDIUM is inflated; corrected to LOW.

survivors.title: cosmetic_class_id_query is page-allowlisted, performs a synchronous WinHTTP call on the browser UI thread, and delivers its result to the ACTIVE tab rather than to the requesting frame
survivors.location: cef-native/src/handlers/simple_handler.cpp:2048 (allowlist), :6552-6596 (arm, note :6581 GetActiveTab); cef-native/include/core/AdblockCache.h:463-468 and the WinHttpOpen/WinHttpConnect block at ~:828-848
survivors.claim: `OnProcessMessageReceived` is CEF_REQUIRE_UI_THREAD (simple_handler.cpp:2058). The cosmetic arm calls `AdblockCache::fetchHiddenIdSelectors` (:6574), which is a blocking WinHTTP round-trip to the adblock engine with 3000 ms connect/send/receive timeouts (AdblockCache.h:463-468, :828-848). A page can drive that in a loop with arbitrarily large `classes`/`ids` arrays, blocking the browser UI thread — which is the same thread that services every tab, every overlay, and the payment modals. Separately, the returned CSS is not sent back to the frame that asked: it is sent to `TabManager::GetInstance().GetActiveTab()` (:6581-6589). The `url` used for the filter lookup is page-supplied (:6560). So a background tab or a subframe can request cosmetic selectors for a domain of its choosing and have them injected into whatever document the user is currently looking at.
survivors.why_it_matters: An allowlisted, 'obviously benign' message is a UI-thread DoS primitive and a cross-tab CSS-injection primitive. The injected payload is display:none rules, so it can hide elements of an unrelated site the user is actively using — including warning text on a confirmation screen. The C2 comment enumerated this name as safe without examining either property.
survivors.how_to_confirm: From a background tab, send cosmetic_class_id_query with a 50k-element `classes` array in a tight loop and measure main-window responsiveness; separately, send it with `url` set to a site with known cosmetic rules while a different site is the active tab, and check whether inject_cosmetic_css arrives at the active tab's renderer. survivors.refuter_reasoning:
I tried to refute on five axes and failed on all five.

CITATIONS CURRENT: allowlist entry is exactly simple_handler.cpp:2048 inside IpcMessageAllowedFromWebPage (:2046). CEF_REQUIRE_UI_THREAD is :2059 (filed :2058). Arm is exactly :6552. fetchHiddenIdSelectors call is :6575 (filed :6574). GetActiveTab is :6582 (filed :6581). AdblockCache.h:463-468 is exact. CefMessageSendHandler::Execute (:51-130) applies no name filtering. The arm has NO IsGlobalEnabled() check, unlike every other adblock call site (:1380, :7732, :8001, :8125) — only g_adblockServerRunning inside fetchHiddenIdSelectors. So the blocking loopback round-trip fires even when the user has ad blocking turned OFF (engine.rs:562-564 returns empty, but the trip still happens). HttpRequestInterceptor.cpp:1801-1805 records the threading rule ("SyncHttpClient calls happen on TID_FILE_USER_BLOCKING workers") and AdblockCache.h:141-144 posts the sibling adblock check off-thread with the comment "Post the blocking HTTP check to a background thread". Of the four allowlisted names, cosmetic_class_id_query is the only one that does a synchronous network round-trip on TID_UI. The project's own convention indicts it.

LABELLING: correct. Filed as CODE_READING, no measurement asserted, none made. Not mislabelled.

PROVENANCE IN SCOPE: AdblockCache.h was not touched in 637e216..HEAD; the arm dates to c2c4e0a. The in-range change is aa439d3, which added the allowlist plus the comment at :2036-2045 asserting these four names are the complete safe set. Blessing-without-examining is squarely in scope for this range.

TWO CORRECTIONS THAT DEFLATE THE "WHY IT MATTERS" (but do not refute):
(1) It cannot reach any Hodos confirmation screen. TabManager.cpp:333-338 GetActiveTab returns a Tab*, and Tab records come only from CreateTab (12 call sites, all window/popup/new-tab creation). Payment modals and BRC-100 auth prompts are separate CEF overlay browsers never registered with TabManager. "warning text on a confirmation screen" is false for any wallet-authored prompt; it applies only to a website's own UI.
(2) The CSS is not attacker-authored. Payload is "<selectors> { display: none !important; }" (simple_render_process_handler.cpp:1136-1150) with backslash/quote/CR/LF escaped — no JS injection. A page can submit a url with no unhide exceptions and force generic hide rules into a document that has adblock exceptions, generichide, or a per-site opt-out — hiding elements the victim site deliberately keeps visible.

The cross-tab CSS half alone is LOW. No funds move on either half. Subject: browser process, HodosBrowserShell, _WIN32 arm plus __APPLE__ arm. Confidence: high on the code reading; the DoS magnitude (how long a loop can pin TID_UI) is unmeasured and would need a harness to quantify.

survivors.title: ResolveIpcOrigin's ancestor cascade upgrades a deliberately-opaque sandboxed frame to its parent's origin, handing the parent's wallet trust to content the parent isolated
survivors.claim: The cascade at :2013-2018 climbs to the nearest ancestor whose URL yields a non-empty authority, on the stated premise that 'about:blank / data: / blob: inherit the nearest real ancestor origin'. That premise is false for sandboxed frames. `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts" srcdoc="...">` has document URL about:srcdoc (OriginFromUrl -> empty) but a fresh OPAQUE origin, not the parent's; the cascade nevertheless returns the parent's authority. Same for `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts" src="/user-content.html">`, where the frame URL is same-origin but the security origin is opaque — here OriginFromUrl returns the parent's authority directly at step 1, no cascade needed. cefMessage is injected into these contexts (simple_render_process_handler.cpp:737 is unconditional). Note the code is *safe* in the direction the prior panel attacked (data:/blob: children of a hostile page still resolve to that hostile page, and a top-level data: document resolves to the opaque-origin.invalid sentinel at :2028-2030 — I could not break that). The failure is the other direction: opaque origins being promoted.
survivors.why_it_matters: Sandboxed srcdoc/iframes are the standard way a site isolates untrusted user-generated content. On an approved dApp, that isolated content is handed the dApp's trust level, per-tx cap and session budget on both transports. The security model says the sandbox strips privileges; Hodos re-grants them.
survivors.how_to_confirm: On an approved dev domain, embed `<iframe sandbox="allow-scripts" srcdoc="<script>cefMessage.send('wallet_call',[...])<\/script>">` and read the browser log's resolved origin for that message. Expect the parent's authority. Negative control: the same frame without the sandbox attribute should resolve identically — if it does, the code is provably not distinguishing the two, which is the finding.
survivors.refuter_reasoning:
CORE MECHANISM SURVIVES, ATTRIBUTION AND SEVERITY REFUTED.

CONFIRMED (could not refute):
- Citations current. ResolveIpcOrigin at cef-native/src/handlers/simple_handler.cpp:2008; cascade comment :2014; sentinel :2028; default-deny gate :2068; allowlist :2046. Code says what they claim.
- Reachability real. cefMessage injected at simple_render_process_handler.cpp:736-741, AFTER the `isInternalPage || isOverlayBrowser` block closes at :733 — unconditional, every V8 context, no main-frame or origin predicate. Their :737 cite is exact. wallet_call is on the 4-name allowlist, so a subframe does reach the money path.
- Their premise-critique is in fact STRONGER than stated: `data:` frames get an opaque origin unconditionally per HTML spec, not only when sandboxed, so the :2014 comment ("data: ... inherit the nearest real ancestor origin") is false on its face. And CefFrame exposes no security-origin accessor in the browser process, so the mismapping is undetectable at this layer. Outcome is robust to what CEF returns for a srcdoc frame (about:srcdoc, empty, or parent URL all land on the parent authority).

REFUTED:
R1 — NOT WHAT LANDED IN THIS RANGE. `git show 637e216:cef-native/src/handlers/simple_handler.cpp | sed -n 2055,2100p` contains the identical cascade, the identical comment "Inherit from the nearest ancestor that has one (about:blank/data:/blob:)", and the identical opaque-origin.invalid sentinel. aa439d3 RELOCATED it to file scope and hardened only the parse (scheme anchoring + userinfo strip). The ancestor logic predates the review base verbatim. Filing this as a defect of what landed is wrong; it is a pre-existing residual.

R2 — TITLE MISLOCATES THE MECHANISM, and the finding's own body concedes it. The `sandbox src="/user-content.html"` half resolves at step 1 with the cascade never entered; changing the cascade fixes nothing there. The true defect statement is "CefFrame::GetURL() is a document URL, not a security origin" — broader, and needing a different fix (renderer-side origin stamping), not a cascade edit.

R3 — DELETING THE CASCADE WOULD BE A REGRESSION. Without it an about:blank child yields empty origin, and IsInternalOrigin("") == true routes the call as fully wallet-internal with no gate at all — the E1 bypass measured 2026-08-19. The finding proposes no replacement that preserves that closure.

R4 — SEVERITY INFLATED. The chain requires ALL of: (a) TrustLevel::Approved — matrix_c.rs:76 prompts for Unknown, so no drive-by site qualifies; (b) the approved dApp embedding attacker-controlled script in a sandboxed frame whose URL is srcdoc/data:/about:blank — a cross-origin `src` resolves to the real child origin correctly, so the common ad/third-party-embed case is unaffected; (c) spend <= per_tx_limit_cents (matrix_c.rs:273, default $1) and <= session cap (default $10); (d) it is NOT invisible — the IPC silent path fires OnWalletCallSuccess at HttpRequestInterceptor.cpp:3065, and OnWalletCallSuccess (:968) emits the gold pill on any auto-approved payment regardless of cents (the `cents <= 0` guard was deliberately removed). The user's primary visual safeguard still fires (misattributed to the parent domain, which is a symptom worth noting, but it fires).

R5 — WITHIN THIS RANGE THE RISK DECREASED. Pre-range the same frame received full internal trust; post-range it receives the parent dApp's capped trust. The reviewed change materially reduced this exposure rather than creating it.

NOT REFUTED ON LABEL: correctly marked CODE_READING. My counter-analysis is also a code reading, plus a `git show` of the base blob (tree history, not runtime). I ran nothing and launched no browser.

NET: keep as a LOW residual/hardening item, re-titled to "frame URL is not the security origin; opaque-origin subframes inherit ancestor authority", with the correction that it predates 637e216. Confidence high on R1/R3/R4 (directly verified in-tree); moderate on the exploit's practical prevalence, which depends on real dApps sandboxing UGC with allow-scripts.

survivors.title: The permission-table gate silently breaks window.yours/window.panda disconnect() — the commit's "verified at every call site" audit missed the injected-JS writer in cef-native itself
survivors.claim: 81c054c's commit message asserts "every legitimate writer is first-party and reaches Rust header-free ... VERIFIED at every call site ... (all /domain/permissions* and /wallet/session-* sites in cef-native checked)". That is false. CWIShimScript.h:548-557 is a call site in cef-native, and it is page-context: `window.yours.disconnect()` / `window.panda.disconnect()` calls `window.__hodos_walletCall('disconnect', '/domain/permissions?domain=' + origin, {}, 'DELETE')`. That rides wallet_call (allowlisted by the C2 IPC gate), reaches HandleIpcWalletCall with an external origin, and runIpcEngineCascade stamps `headers["X-Requesting-Domain"] = origin` (HttpRequestInterceptor.cpp:2069). domain_trust_mw now sees method=DELETE and path.starts_with("/domain/permissions") and returns 403 permission_table_is_first_party_only. The shim maps the rejection to `return false` (CWIShimScript.h:557: `.then(function(){return true;}, function(){return false;})`), so the site gets a plain falsy return, not an error. The audit checked the C++ HTTP call sites (DomainPermissionTask, AdvancedDomainPermissionTask, the two SyncHttpClient::Post writes, ScopedGrantTask, approve_cert_fields, fireSessionApprove/RevokeToRust — all genuinely header-free, I verified each) but not the JS the browser injects into pages.
survivors.why_it_matters: disconnect() is a de-escalation, the one permission-table mutation a site has a legitimate reason to make. A user who clicks "Disconnect" in a dApp now gets a UI that says disconnected while Hodos keeps trust_level=approved, the per-tx/per-session spending caps, and any identityKeyDisclosureAllowed=1 flag. That is a money-path trust divergence: the site retains silent-spend authority up to caps after the user believes it was revoked. It also means the phase's blanket-gate rationale ("every legitimate writer is first-party") is not the invariant it claims to be, so the next person reasoning from it will be reasoning from a false premise.
survivors.how_to_confirm: With the dev wallet running, load any https dApp, approve it once, then from its console run `await window.yours.disconnect()`. Expect `false`, a wallet log line `🛡️ REFUSED DELETE /domain/permissions from dApp origin '<host>'`, and the row still present in domain_permissions. Negative control: revert only the main.rs:106-119 block, rebuild, repeat — expect `true` and the row gone. (Do it against an APPROVED domain; an unapproved one is stopped earlier by domain_trust_gate with a 202, which would false-green the test — the same trap that voided the first C3 measurement.)
survivors.refuter_reasoning: I could not refute the mechanism. Origin format matches the stored key (hodos::OriginFromUrl, PortConfig.h:104-122, returns authority only == window.location.host), and pre-fix an approved domain hit Proceed (request_gate.rs:807-809) and reached delete_domain_permission (handlers.rs:10233-10263). survivors.title: The three request->SetURL() rewrites in GetResourceHandler are no-ops per the CEF contract — the interop fix is credited to a mechanism that cannot fire
survivors.claim: cef_resource_request_handler.h:104 states of GetResourceHandler: "The |request| object cannot not be modified in this callback." (sic — double negative, meaning it is read-only there; CefRequestImpl setters no-op on a read-only request in release). All three SetURL calls in HttpRequestInterceptor::GetResourceHandler are therefore inert on the wire. The interop fix in 9b73bd7 nevertheless works, because the *local* `url` variable carries the rewrite into isWalletEndpoint(url) and the endpoint extraction at :3922-3928, and AsyncWalletResourceHandler then dials hodos::WalletBaseUrl() + endpoint itself. So the wallet gets the call from the handler, not from the redirect. The commit's evidence lines ("-> http://localhost:31401/getVersion") are LOG_DEBUG strings emitted unconditionally next to the inert SetURL; the only load-bearing observation is the wallet's `POST /getVersion 200`, which the handler path fully explains. Consequence: the guard comment at :3772-3774 ("⛔ Downgrade ONLY once the URL is already OUR wallet host:port ... this must not become a general https->http rewrite") is guarding an operation that does not reach the network, while the thing it does affect — which URLs isWalletEndpoint matches — is not what the comment describes.
survivors.why_it_matters: Two branches, both worth knowing. If SetURL is inert as documented, a maintainer who later moves this logic to OnBeforeResourceLoad (where SetURL DOES work) inherits a real https->http downgrade keyed on an unanchored substring, and the redirectPort arm starts silently retargeting any 127.0.0.1:8080 navigation at the wallet port. If SetURL is NOT inert in our CEF 150 build, then 9b73bd7's widening of the 8080 arm to the 127.0.0.1 spelling (simple_handler.cpp:8190) already breaks browsing to any local service on 127.0.0.1:8080 — the default spelling for most dev servers — because that URL is rewritten to the wallet port and then falls through isWalletEndpoint to "allowing normal processing". Either way the recorded mechanism for a shipped fix is wrong.
survivors.how_to_confirm: One experiment settles both branches: run any local server on 127.0.0.1:8080 (`python -m http.server 8080`), then navigate Hodos to http://127.0.0.1:8080/. If the page loads, SetURL is inert (finding is doc/mechanism-only). If you get the wallet's response or a connection failure to 31301/31401, SetURL is live and the 8080 widening is a shipped browsing regression. Do NOT use localhost:8080 for this — that spelling was already matched pre-range and would not discriminate.

survivors.title: The new /health arm's "scoped to our own host:port" protection is an unanchored substring — the exact defect class C1 just fixed for origins
survivors.claim: The arm reads `if (hodos::IsWalletHostPort(url) && url.find("/health") != npos) return true;` and its comment claims it is "SCOPED to our own host:port ON PURPOSE ... unscoped it would hijack the health endpoint of every ordinary website". But IsWalletHostPort is `url.find("127.0.0.1:31301") != npos || url.find("localhost:31301") != npos` — an unanchored search of the whole URL, including the query string the page author controls. So `https://any.site/health?x=127.0.0.1:31301` satisfies both conditions: SimpleHandler::GetResourceRequestHandler (simple_handler.cpp:8187) attaches the interceptor on the same substring, isWalletEndpoint returns true, endpoint is extracted as `/health?x=127.0.0.1:31301` (HttpRequestInterceptor.cpp:3922-3928), and AsyncWalletResourceHandler serves the wallet's /health response to that site's own same-origin fetch — bypassing the Rust CORS layer entirely, since the response is synthesized locally. This is the identical shape C1 documented and fixed for the origin derivation (PortConfig.h:60-70: "an unanchored substring search for the host:port admits any URL that merely CONTAINS it, anywhere - including in a query string the page author controls").
survivors.why_it_matters: Impact today is nil in itself — handlers::health (rust-wallet/src/handlers.rs:178-184) returns a static {status, version, backend} JSON with no secrets. The value of reporting it is that the comment asserts a scoping guarantee the code does not provide, so the next host-qualified arm added on the same pattern (or any growth of /health into a status/balance probe) inherits a page-triggerable route into the wallet. It also means a site whose own /health URL happens to carry the wallet host:port becomes unreachable.
survivors.how_to_confirm: From any https page's console: `await (await fetch('/health?x=127.0.0.1:31301')).json()`. Expect the wallet's {"status":"ok","backend":"rust-wallet"} rather than the site's own /health. Negative control: same fetch without the query parameter — expect the site's real response (or 404). Use the release port for the release build; 31401 under HODOS_DEV=1.
survivors.refuter_reasoning:
I could not refute the mechanics, but the framing and attribution are wrong, and the severity should drop to INFO. All of this is CODE_READING — I ran no browser, sent no request, and I did not build. (a) Could this pass with the feature removed? N/A — no test was run by the filer or by me; nothing is being claimed green. (b) SUBJECT: source tree at HEAD (5b5bf44) on branch 0.4.0, browser-process C++ (SimpleHandler / HttpRequestInterceptor), not a running binary. (c) If it were broken you would see the log line "🌐 Not a wallet endpoint, allowing normal processing" for the crafted URL; nobody looked, and nobody claims to have. (d) CODE_READING, correctly labelled by the filer.

CITATIONS VERIFIED CURRENT (I re-grepped every one):
- cef-native/src/core/HttpRequestInterceptor.cpp:5117 — `if (hodos::IsWalletHostPort(url) && url.find("/health") != std::string::npos) return true;` with the "SCOPED to our own host:port ON PURPOSE" comment at 5112-5116. Exact.
- cef-native/include/core/PortConfig.h:161-165 — `IsWalletHostPort` is indeed `url.find("localhost:"+p) || url.find("127.0.0.1:"+p)`, unanchored over the whole URL. Exact.
- Chain: attach at simple_handler.cpp:8187-8194 (`hodos::IsWalletHostPort(url) || ... return new HttpRequestInterceptor()`), endpoint extraction at HttpRequestInterceptor.cpp:3922-3928, forward at 3588 (`fullUrl = hodos::WalletBaseUrl() + endpoint_`), so `/health?x=127.0.0.1:31301` reaches actix's `/health` route (rust-wallet/src/main.rs:1032 → handlers.rs:178-184, static JSON). Mechanically the chain holds.

WHERE THE FINDING IS WRONG:

1. MIS-ATTRIBUTION — this is not "the new /health arm's" defect and it is not new. The unanchored predicate is `IsWalletHostPort`, which also gates whether the interceptor attaches at all (simple_handler.cpp:8187). `git log -S` shows the helper landed in 4ba4fe7 (PRE-range) and before that the same gate was a literal `find("localhost:31301")` dating to the initial commit cc6cf19. Consequence: every pre-existing bare-path arm — `/wallet/`, `/transaction/`, `/createAction` — is reachable by the identical query-string trick (`https://evil.com/wallet/anything?x=127.0.0.1:31301`) and has been for the life of the product. The /health arm therefore does not weaken anything; it is the only arm carrying an EXTRA condition on top of a gate that was already substring-based. Filing it against 9b73bd7's arm points the next reader at the wrong line to fix. The fix belongs in PortConfig.h:161 (or at the attach site), not in isWalletEndpoint.

2. THE C1 ANALOGY IS ONLY HALF RIGHT, and that half is what sets severity. C1's derivation was a TRUST-ELEVATION gate: matching there made a frame wallet-internal (hodosBrowser injection, header-free first-party calls). Matching here grants ROUTING ONLY. extractDomain (HttpRequestInterceptor.cpp:3979, 5173-5193) reads the MAIN FRAME url, so the forwarded request carries `X-Requesting-Domain: evil.com` (3596-3599), and d0ee6db's denylist (3629-3660) prevents the page from overwriting it. So the crafted request is gated by domain_trust_mw exactly like any ordinary third-party wallet call. There is no privilege gain — only a same-origin-shaped response that skips browser CORS. Calling it "the identical shape" inflates the class.

3. A GATE THEY MISSED (partial, not fatal). simple_handler.cpp:8121-8163 runs adblock BEFORE the wallet-attach branch: on `CacheResult::MISS` it returns `DeferredAdblockHandler`, whose GetResourceHandler only does InstallAsync402HandlerIfPending (AdblockCache.h:164-171) — so the FIRST fetch of that URL goes to the real network and never sees isWalletEndpoint. Interception only happens once the URL is cached HIT_ALLOWED (i.e. the second identical fetch), or with adblock disabled. Trivial to satisfy, but the filed chain is not the whole story and was presented as if it were.

4. THE COMMENT IS WRONG IN A DIFFERENT WAY THAN CLAIMED. Even fully unscoped, this arm could not "hijack the health endpoint of every ordinary website" — the interceptor never attaches to ordinary sites (8187-8193 requires the wallet host:port, 3321/2121/8080, messagebox, or /.well-known/auth). So the comment overstates its threat, rather than overstating its protection.

NET: mechanics CONFIRMED, so it survives — but as an INFO-grade note on a PRE-EXISTING shared predicate (`IsWalletHostPort` should be authority-anchored the way `IsInternalFrontendUrl` now is), not as a LOW defect in the /health arm. Impact today is nil by the filer's own admission (static {status,version,backend}), there is no trust escalation, and the "next arm inherits it" hazard is real but already inherited by ~20 existing arms. Confidence high on the code reading; I did not execute anything.

Incidental, higher-value and NOT in the finding: the same unanchored predicate reaches HttpRequestInterceptor.cpp:3770-3775, the https→http rewrite added by 9b73bd7 whose own comment says "this must not become a general https->http rewrite". `https://bank.com/api?u=127.0.0.1:31301` attaches the interceptor, gets `request->SetURL()` downgraded to http://, and if no isWalletEndpoint arm matches, falls through to CEF with the DOWNGRADED url. Mixed-content blocking likely fails it closed, so probably not exploitable, but that is the arm actually worth re-examining — not /health. CODE_READING, confidence medium, filed here only as a pointer.

survivors.title: Latent: the direct-HTTP transport stamps X-Requesting-Domain for INTERNAL origins too, so the first wallet-UI direct fetch anyone re-adds will be treated as a dApp
survivors.location: cef-native/src/core/HttpRequestInterceptor.cpp:3597-3599 (stamps unconditionally on requestDomain_); :2240-2245 (Open()'s internal bypass leaves requestDomain_ populated)
survivors.claim: AsyncWalletResourceHandler::startAsyncHTTPRequest stamps `X-Requesting-Domain: <requestDomain_>` whenever requestDomain_ is non-empty, with no IsInternalOrigin check. requestDomain_ comes from extractDomain(browser, request), so an internal page's direct fetch to the wallet would arrive at Rust carrying `X-Requesting-Domain: 127.0.0.1:5137`. Rust would then treat the user's own UI as an untrusted domain: domain_trust_gate would 202 a connect prompt for it, and the new gate at main.rs:110 would 403 any /domain/permissions or /wallet/session-* write from it. The IPC path deliberately does NOT do this — runIpcCallDirect at :1942-1943 stamps only `if (!origin.empty() && !IsInternalOrigin(origin))`, with a comment naming exactly this failure ("Stamping the loopback origin here is exactly the 'naive break' that 403s wallet_backup/wallet_export and prompts the user for their own identity key"). The two transports disagree, and only one of them has the guard. This is dormant today: I grepped frontend/src for :31301/:31401 and for non-walletFetch fetch() calls and found zero direct wallet fetches — walletApi.ts routes 100% through __hodos_walletCall.

survivors.how_to_confirm: Add a throwaway `fetch('http://127.0.0.1:31401/domain/permissions', {method:'POST', body:'{...}'} )` from an overlay page in a dev build and watch the wallet log for `🛡️ REFUSED POST /domain/permissions from dApp origin '127.0.0.1:5137'`. === CORRECTION 3 (the filer UNDERSTATED the mechanism — this is the strongest part of the finding) ===

With the schema default that makes a mempool-only recovered output IMMEDIATELY eligible as a createAction input — which is precisely what that clause exists to prevent. The defect is therefore not only "the reaper is blind"; it also admits an unconfirmed external receive straight into input selection on the very next spend. Had the correct flag been written, line 83 would have excluded it until confirmation.

=== CORRECTION 4 (framing) ===
The "since 293f269" framing is only half right. I read the pre-image (`git show 293f269^:rust-wallet/src/utxo_fetcher.rs`): `fetch_utxos_woc` already hit `/unspent/all` and already computed `let confirmed = u.height > 0;` BEFORE 293f269, and fetch_utxos_bulk's single-address fallback routes through it. So this is not a regression 4eacb51 introduced-and-missed, it is a pre-existing defect of the same class that 4eacb51's file-scoped audit did not reach. The filer's headline ("the audit was file-scoped, not dataflow-scoped") is fair; "reproduces verbatim the defect 4eacb51 was written to eliminate" is fair as to CLASS, not as to provenance.

=== ADJACENT, FLAGGED SO IT IS NOT RE-DERIVED (low confidence, not filed) ===
handlers.rs:15932 records a JUST-BROADCAST sweep output via the plain `upsert_received_utxo`, which hardcodes confirmed=true (output_repo.rs:425-435). handlers.rs:14343 does the same for backup change. Both are unconfirmed at the instant of insert. Same class, different dataflow, pre-existing, out of this finding's scope.

=== SEVERITY REASONING ===
Impact is real and the code path is proven. But harm is conjunctive: (1) the user takes the restore fallback or an approved dApp POSTs rescan, AND (2) a receive is sitting in the mempool at that instant, AND (3) that parent tx never confirms (eviction / double-spend). Step 3 is uncommon on BSV. Compare the precedent: 4eacb51 fixed the identical defect on the bulk tier, which runs automatically every 5 minutes for every user — near-certain exposure. This path is an order of magnitude rarer. Same impact, much lower probability => MEDIUM. I would not fight HIGH if the owner weights "wallet_recover is the restore path and a phantom output there needs a manual DB fix to clear", but on this panel's own risk calculus MEDIUM is the honest number. The fix is a one-line signature change (thread `utxo.confirmed` through upsert_received_utxo_with_derivation), so the cost/benefit argues for fixing it now regardless of the label.

"breaks with no error anywhere" is FALSE, and this is the load-bearing premise of the whole "ships broken, discovered by users" argument. simple_handler.cpp:2069 emits `LOG_WARNING_BROWSER("🛡️ IPC DENIED: '" + message_name + "' from external origin '" + ipcOrigin + "' …")` — it names the exact rejected message AND the origin. And Logger has NO level filter whatsoever: `Logger::Log` (cef-native/src/core/Logger.cpp:30-54) writes every entry to the file and stdout with no threshold; `Logger::Initialize` is called unconditionally at cef_browser_shell.cpp:4601, not dev-gated. The project's own TICKET_production_debug_logging_unbounded.md independently proves release builds log at DEBUG into a 1.58 GB `%APPDATA%\HodosBrowser\logs\debug_output.log`. A fifth name would announce itself by name in the shipping log on first occurrence. The failure is loud, not silent.

B. "the page just hangs" is true only for `wallet_call`, which is ON the allowlist. cosmetic_class_id_query / find_result_js / qr_found are fire-and-forget; over-blocking them degrades a feature, it does not hang a page.

C. The failure direction is FAIL-CLOSED, which inverts the severity band. C2's security property is default-deny; allowlist COMPLETENESS is a functionality claim, not a security claim. An incomplete allowlist makes the trust boundary STRICTER. It cannot lose money, cannot cross the trust boundary, cannot touch the first-party UI (the gate only fires when `!IsInternalOrigin(ipcOrigin)`). A mislabelled-but-TRUE claim whose only error direction is fail-closed does not belong at HIGH.

D. The filer understates the control that WAS run. §4j's 0.5a table measured all four allowlisted names from a real external origin — `find_result_js`, `qr_found`, `cosmetic_class_id_query` dispatched with no denial; `wallet_call` exercised throughout findings 4/5/6 and again in §4k against a real third-party dApp. Every name that actually exists was positively observed passing the gate. CITATION DRIFT IN THE FINDING ITSELF
- "simple_render_process_handler.cpp:553" for the internal-page gate is STALE. The gate is `if (isInternalPage || isOverlayBrowser)` at :587 (and again :784). :553 is inside a chrome-stub string.
- "simple_handler.cpp:2046-2052" points at the helper, not the enforcement site (:2068-2071). Minor, but this panel's own rules make it worth naming.

ON THE LABEL ITSELF (the part I most nearly refuted)
The paragraph's first clause after the headline is literally "Re-derived from scratch: all `CefProcessMessage::Create` sites split by process…" and it then explicitly partitions off the measured sub-claim ("`find_result_js` and `qr_found` had never been exercised and are now measured passing"). A reader cannot be misled about what produced the universal claim. HARNESS §6(d)'s actual harm — someone treating an unverified reading as an observed fact — does not obtain. That said, the doc proves the author knows the compound form (PHASE_CONTRACT.md:286 reads "**MEASUREMENT + CODE READING, 2026-08-19.**") and chose the bare MEASUREMENT banner here, so a one-word inconsistency is genuine.

VERDICT: keep it, as a LOW documentation/process item with a concrete cheap remedy — retitle §4j "MEASUREMENT + CODE READING" and run the 5-minute Minimal basket (youtube/x/github), then `grep "IPC DENIED" debug_output.log`. Note the negative control is free and the filer missed it: the log line at :2069 makes the basket run self-scoring, and a bad basket run would go red for the right reason with the message name printed. Do NOT let this block sign-off ahead of the still-open `G1` release-shaped build. Confidence: high on A–D (all directly verified in current source); moderate on the label critique (a judgement call about doc vocabulary, not a fact).

Evidence kind: CODE_READING throughout. I ran git/grep/sed only. I did not launch the browser, drive CDP, or spend anything.

survivors.title: The /health arm's "host-qualified" guard is an unanchored substring — an EXTERNAL host's /health does route to the wallet

This arm must stay host-qualified" (HttpRequestInterceptor.cpp:5110-5116) — is not enforced. `hodos::IsWalletHostPort` (PortConfig.h:161-165) is `url.find("localhost:31401") || url.find("127.0.0.1:31401")` over the WHOLE URL string, including path, query and fragment. It is not an authority test. Worse, `redirectPort` at :3755-3762 also searches the whole URL, so it will MANUFACTURE the qualifying substring out of attacker-controlled query text. Full chain for `https://example.com/health?x=127.0.0.1:8080`: (1) simple_handler.cpp:8190 `IsLoopbackHostPort(url,"8080")` matches the query → HttpRequestInterceptor attached; (2) redirectPort rewrites the QUERY `127.0.0.1:8080` → `127.0.0.1:31401`; (3) :3773 downgrade fires; (4) :5117 `IsWalletHostPort` now true and `/health` present → isWalletEndpoint returns true; (5) :3921-3929 extracts `endpoint = "/health?x=..."` and :3588 builds `fullUrl = hodos::WalletBaseUrl() + endpoint_` — the host `example.com` is DISCARDED. The page's request to example.com is answered by our wallet. The identical inversion was found, fixed and unit-tested four days earlier in this same header: port_config_origin_test.cpp:128 asserts `EXPECT_FALSE(IsInternalFrontendUrl("https://example.com/?x=127.0.0.1:5137"))`.

Direct disclosure is small (/health returns only {status,version,backend}, handlers.rs:178-184), but the guard is now believed-safe and will be reused as precedent for the next scoped arm — and the same three-line chain promotes ANY external URL into 'this is our wallet host' for every other IsWalletHostPort consumer.
survivors.how_to_confirm: Unit test, no browser needed: add to cef-native/tests/port_config_origin_test.cpp `EXPECT_FALSE(hodos::IsWalletHostPort("https://example.com/health?x=127.0.0.1:31401"));` — it will fail. Then end-to-end: load a page that does `fetch('https://<any-host-you-control>/health?x=127.0.0.1:8080')` and confirm the reply body is `{"backend":"rust-wallet"}` rather than your server's. survivors.title: Intercepting 127.0.0.1:8080 hijacks the user's own local dev server on the most common local port — and /health makes it likely
survivors.claim: Before 9b73bd7 only the literal `localhost:8080` matched; now `IsLoopbackHostPort(url,"8080")` matches the 127.0.0.1 spelling too, so BOTH spellings of a user's own dev server are routed into HttpRequestInterceptor. For `http://127.0.0.1:8080/health`: the outer gate matches, redirectPort rewrites host:port to 31401, and the new :5117 arm returns true → the request is served by the Hodos wallet, not by the dev server. This is not limited to /health: the pre-existing table at :5122-5159 contains very generic bare substrings — `/encrypt`, `/decrypt`, `/sendMessage`, `/listMessages`, `/transaction/`, `/wallet/`, `/getVersion` — so any of those paths on a local 8080 server are hijacked in both spellings. Second-order: the hijacked call carries `X-Requesting-Domain: 127.0.0.1:8080` (extractDomain, :3979 → :5175-5196 returns main-frame host:port), and domain_trust_mw (rust-wallet/src/main.rs:59-147) has NO endpoint or loopback exemption, so an unknown-trust 127.0.0.1:8080 gets a 202 pending envelope → a wallet CONNECT MODAL pops while the developer is testing their own app, and rust-wallet/src/permission_service/request_gate.rs:815 fires an outbound `fetch_manifest("127.0.0.1:8080")`.
survivors.why_it_matters: 8080 is not a wallet bridge; it is the default port of Spring Boot, Tomcat, http-server, many Docker images, and countless dev setups, and `/health` is the canonical liveness path on exactly those stacks. A developer using Hodos sees their own endpoint silently answered by the wallet plus an unexplained connect prompt. It is also the least defensible entry in the gate: 3321 and 2121 are deliberate product decisions; 8080 is a guess.
survivors.how_to_confirm: Run any static server on 127.0.0.1:8080 exposing /health, browse to it in Hodos, and diff the response body against curl. Then check whether plain browsing works at all: navigate to `http://127.0.0.1:8080/` and see whether you get the dev server or the wallet root — that single navigation also settles whether `request->SetURL()` in GetResourceHandler is honored (see the next finding). Negative control: drop the 8080 arm from simple_handler.cpp:8190 and confirm the hijack stops.
survivors.refuter_reasoning:

CITATIONS VERIFIED CURRENT (all exact): simple_handler.cpp:8190 = `hodos::IsLoopbackHostPort(url, "8080") ||`. The finding's title attributes long-standing behavior to this range.

CONFIDENCE: high on all code readings; I read the current tree and the CEF source, ran nothing.

survivors.title: The https→http downgrade's own guard comment is false, and the downgrade appears to be unnecessary in the first place

survivors.why_it_matters: If CEF ever honors SetURL here (or someone moves this logic to OnBeforeResourceLoad, which is the documented place for it), this becomes a page-triggerable TLS strip on arbitrary third-party https URLs. PARTIALLY SURVIVES — the substantive half (b) is confirmed and strengthened; the security half (a) is refuted; severity is inflated from MEDIUM to LOW.

CITATIONS VERIFIED CURRENT. The commit's "MEASURED 2026-08-19 ... scheme intact" is a reading of that log line, not a wire observation — it is the classic false-green shape the harness rule targets. The actual causes of "Bridge unavailable" were defect #1 (host-form gap, simple_handler.cpp) and defect #3 (/health absent from isWalletEndpoint). The panelist is right that the stated causal story is unsupported by :3588.

SURVIVES — part (a) as a DOCUMENTATION defect only. The "⛔ Downgrade ONLY once the URL is already OUR wallet host:port" annotation is false as written: because IsWalletHostPort is a whole-string substring test, an example.com URL carrying the port in its query satisfies it and the downgrade does fire on the local variable. SEVERITY. MEDIUM is inflated. No web page can produce any wire effect; the code is provably inert in release. It cannot be "masking" anything either — an inert hunk masks nothing. What remains is (i) a false ⛔ comment on dead code, (ii) an unverified causal claim in a commit message that could send a future session chasing a TLS theory that :3588 rules out. Both are real and worth a docs/comment correction, neither is a money-path or trust-boundary risk. LOW.

LABELLING. Honest — filed as CODE_READING, and it is one. No mislabelling. Confidence: HIGH on the libcef read-only chain and the scheme-agnostic downstream audit (both read directly from source in this tree); HIGH on the upstream gate refutation.
